gap: No result ChatGPT got states that neither of its two cards can be bought for a plug-in setup in most of the US: Anker's US SOLIX store lists no Solarbank at all. EcoFlow says STREAM Ultra is 'only available for sale and plug-and-play installation in Utah', and one Ultra exports at most 800 W to the grid. Reaching 1,200 W takes the separate STREAM Microinverter or 2–6 Ultra units, and its DELTA power stations can't be paired with it yet ('available soon').
standout_why: ChatGPT's saved chat ran no searches and got no result pages, so no rival page cites any of this. Its answer offers 'Anker SOLIX Solarbank and EcoFlow STREAM' as popular examples without saying where they are sold. Anker's US site has no Solarbank, and EcoFlow's US page limits STREAM to Utah. Our current page already says 'Utah only' for STREAM Ultra. New here: Solarbank isn't sold in the US, the 800 W single-unit grid limit versus 1,200 W with the microinverter or 2–6 units, DELTA pairing not available yet, and the Shelly Pro 3EM meter EcoFlow recommends when there's no net metering.
decides: Both products ChatGPT showed drop out for a US apartment shopper outside Utah: Solarbank isn't sold in the US and STREAM is Utah-only. That supports leading with off-grid power-station kits that need no grid connection. The BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 200 W kit ($1,199 today) is the stronger pick because its solar input takes 1,000 W at 12–60 V / 20 A, against the AC180's 500 W, 12–60 V and 10 A. A shopper who later adds panels can grow the Elite 200 V2 to 1,000 W, while the AC180 stops at 500 W. STREAM Ultra stays a pick for Utah renters only.
